title: SLO-aware curated evacuation and drain advisor for Dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Fleet maintenance (node upgrades, security patching, and hardware replacement) currently relies on simplistic drain heuristics that can cause transient SLO violations for customers with throughput guarantees. We need a controller (Drain Advisor) that recommends and executes curated evacuation plans for nodes: preserving per-tenant throughput contracts, warming KV caches for rolled traffic, and coordinating with the autoscaler and routing layers.

Goal: Build an SLO-aware evacuation advisor service that: 1) computes safe drain rates per host given active throughput reservations and current observed tail latency; 2) emits drain hints with time windows and prewarm instructions for KV cache; 3) interfaces with autoscaler to reserve temporary capacity or trigger burst lanes; 4) provides actionable playbooks (soft-drain, hard-drain, cancel) and observability in Console.

Success criteria: measurable reduction in transient 95th/99th percentile latency spikes during maintenance events, automated drain execution for low-risk hosts, and manual override flow for complex tenant contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Drain Advisor exposes an API to request a curated evacuation plan for a host and returns: safe_drain_rate, time_window, prewarm_steps, fallback_model_variant
For a representative dedicated fleet benchmark, end-to-end maintenance events do not increase 95th p99 token latency for high-throughput tenants by more than 10% compared to baseline
Advisor integrates with autoscaler: when safe_drain_rate cannot be satisfied, it will request a short-lived capacity reservation and the routing layer will honor burst leases
KV cache prewarm instructions reduce cold-KV tail latency by at least 30% during staged handoffs
Console surfaces drain plans and an audit trail; on-call can abort or throttle an active evacuation with a single action
design_notes: Controller model: hybrid planner + reactive telemetry. Planner computes initial schedule from contracts and traffic distribution; reactive agent adjusts windows using live latency and queue-length signals.

Safe drain rate derivation: use percentile-based throughput headroom per tenant (advertised SLA - observed 95th) and allocate evacuation bandwidth proportional to tenant weight, with global cap to avoid cluster overload.
KV prewarm strategy: push KV prefix population tasks to candidate hosts ahead of traffic handoff; use probabilistic sampling to minimize warmup work for tenants with low QPS.

Autoscaler integration: define a short-lived 'evacuation_reservation' API that requests capacity for a specific maintenance window (duration, vGPU type, model variants). Reservation is charged to node-owner project and subject to policy limits.
Safety nets: staged handoff with canary fraction, fallback to lower-cost model variants if reservation denied, and automatic pause if tail latency threshold breached during handoff.
Trade-offs considered: heavy prewarm reduces tail latency but costs more; the advisor will provide cost vs. latency tradeoff preset (conservative, balanced, aggressive).
Data model: record per-evacuation plan: plan_id, host, affected_tenants (hashed), safe_drain_rate, windows, prewarm_tokens, autoscaler_reservation_id, status. (Stored in control plane DB).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 - Planner MVP (2 sprints): implement planner service that computes safe_drain_rate and produces JSON plan; add simple UI in Console to review/approve; wire audit log entries.
Phase 2 - Reactive agent + KV prewarm (3 sprints): agent runs on hosts, enforces plan, reports telemetry; implement KV prewarm job API and soft-handoff flow.
Phase 3 - Autoscaler & routing integration (2 sprints): add evacuation_reservation API and routing honor logic for burst leases; implement rollback/abort flows.
Phase 4 - Canary + metrics/alerts (1 sprint): run canaries against dedicated fleets, collect SLO metrics, tune thresholds, and document runbook.
Implementation tasks: schema for plan records, Planner service (Go), Agent changes (C++/Rust runtime footprint), autoscaler hook, Console UI changes, e2e tests and stress harness in perf lab.
rollout_plan: Start with internal dedicated testbeds (non-production) and a small set of pilot customers who opt-in to 'curated evacuation' feature.

Phase canary: enable plan generation only (read-only) for 1 week and collect feedback; then enable non-destructive dry-run agent to simulate handoffs; finally enable live execution behind kill-switch.
Monitoring: dashboards for plan success rate, handoff-induced latency delta, autoscaler reservation frequency, and KV warmup hit-rate. Set automated rollback on sustained p99 degradation > 20%.
Communication: notify Solutions & SRE teams before enabling on any Dedicated fleet; publish playbook and runbook in Confluence.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Planner underestimates load and causes SLO breach. Mitigation: conservative default presets, progressive ramp with canary fraction, and immediate auto-pause on threshold breach.
Risk: KV prewarm creates large IO spikes. Mitigation: rate-limit prewarm tasks, prioritize tenants by QPS, and allow operator to switch to 'no-prewarm' mode for low-risk windows.
Risk: Autoscaler reservation not honored due to capacity scarcity. Mitigation: fallback model variant routing, staggered maintenance windows, and operator alerting to reschedule.
Risk: Complexity of tenant contracts (multi-tenant reservations). Mitigation: advisor supports tenant-hash grouping and per-tenant opt-out; surface conflicts in UI for manual resolution.
